In [[algebraic group]] theory, a '''wonderful compactification''' of a variety acted on by an algebraic group <math>G</math> is a <math>G</math>-equivariant [[compactification (mathematics)|compactification]] such that the [[closure (topology)|closure]] of each [[Orbit (group theory)#Orbits and stabilizers|orbit]] is smooth.   {{harvs|txt | last1=de Concini | first1=Corrado | author1-link=Corrado de Concini | last2=Procesi | first2=Claudio | author2-link=Claudio Procesi | editor1-last=Gherardelli | editor1-first=Francesco | title=Invariant theory (Montecatini, 1982) | url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1007/BFb0063234 | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | location=Berlin, New York | series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics | isbn=978-3-540-12319-4 | doi=10.1007/BFb0063234 |mr=718125 | year=1983 | volume=996 | chapter=Complete symmetric varieties | pages=1–44}} constructed a wonderful compactification of any [[symmetric variety]] given by a [[quotient group|quotient]] <math>G/G^{\sigma}</math> of an algebraic group <math>G</math> by the subgroup  <math>G^{\sigma}</math> fixed by some involution <math>\sigma</math> of <math>G</math> over the [[complex number]]s, sometimes called the '''De Concini–Procesi compactification'''. {{harvs|txt|last=Strickland|
first=Elisabetta| year=1987}} generalized this construction to arbitrary characteristic. In particular, by writing a group <math>G</math> itself as a symmetric homogeneous space, <math>G=(G \times G)/G</math> (modulo the diagonal subgroup), this gives a wonderful compactification of the group <math>G</math> itself.
